pages.title: About Kiban Structural
pages.content:
ABOUT

About Kiban Structural

Home / About

Founded in 2009 by Mara Lindqvist, Kiban Structural is an independent structural engineering practice based at Calder Quay. We combine contractor-side practical experience with analytical design rigor across residential, commercial, and civic buildings.

2009

Year founded

7

People in the studio

6

Stages on every job

Founding and Contractor-Side Experience

Mara Lindqvist established Kiban Structural in 2009 following twelve years working directly within contractor design teams on complex commercial and residential developments. That on-site background continues to guide how our studio operates today. We understand that structural calculations are only as robust as their execution on the building site. Practical structural engineering must never be divorced from constructability, realistic trade tolerances, erection sequences, and safe site access. Every scheme we develop balances rigorous mathematical modeling with buildable details.

The Principle of Foundation

Our name originates from the Japanese word for foundation. It represents the quiet, solid ground upon which every architectural form and operational requirement depends. We believe sound engineering begins with humble inquiry: interrogating site boundaries, verifying soil strata, and establishing realistic load take-downs before drafting commences. By resolving structural challenges early within the schematic phase, we provide architects and builders with a dependable technical baseline that prevents structural surprises and costly redesigns.

Working with Architects and Developers

We work alongside architects and developers from the initial feasibility stage through to final completion. Each project is assigned one named chartered structural engineer who acts as the dedicated technical contact throughout the job. Instead of passing projects through anonymous departments, our single-engineer accountability ensures that structural intent remains intact across design revisions, site coordination meetings, and unexpected existing conditions discovered during construction. We deliver early scheme notes that clarify options before major commitments are locked.

Calder Quay Studio and Verification Scope

Founded in 2009, our Calder Quay studio maintains a team of 7 people delivering structural design across a disciplined 6-stage engineering process. We operate strictly to Eurocodes and ISO 19650 information standards. Our work covers new reinforced concrete frames, mass timber structures, fabricated steel trusses, and complex masonry retrofits. Every calculation package is reviewed internally by an independent checking engineer before being signed and released for statutory building authority submission.

pages.title: Structural Engineering Services
pages.content:
SERVICES

Structural Engineering Services

Home / Services

Kiban Structural delivers structural design, independent calculation checks, and condition appraisals for architects, developers, and building owners. Our work is delivered across three core services backed by clear schedules and fixed milestones.

Structural Design for New Buildings

Our primary service covers comprehensive structural engineering design for new construction, ranging from multi-storey residential frames to civic buildings. Deliverables include a preliminary structural scheme note, finite element modeling, framing layouts, general arrangement drawings, foundation designs, and signed calculation packages for regulatory approval. A typical design program requires two to four weeks for computer modeling and two to three weeks for detailed drawing production. For residential projects up to four storeys, our fee begins from €9,500, with initial feasibility notes from €1,800.

Independent Structural Design Checking

We provide rigorous third-party independent checks for complex structural frames, timber systems, and foundation schemes designed by external engineering teams. Deliverables include an independent verification model created from primary architectural drawings, member capacity checks, serviceability deflection evaluations, and a formal written checking commentary. This service typically requires one to two weeks depending on structural complexity. Our independent design checks are offered from €3,200, delivering the objective oversight required by statutory building authorities and institutional project insurers.

Retrofit Assessment and Condition Review

We evaluate existing buildings, historic masonry structures, and industrial warehouses to determine load capacity and detail strengthening works. Deliverables comprise an initial site survey, measured defect records, foundation appraisal, secondary framing design, and installation sequence notes. Survey work is billed at €950 per site day, with retrofit assessment and strengthening design priced from €4,800. Regular site inspection visits accompanied by a written engineering report are available at €640 per visit, ensuring alterations remain structurally sound throughout construction.

pages.title: Process and Methodology
pages.content:
PROCESS

Process and Methodology

Home / Process

Every commission at Kiban Structural follows a sequential six-stage process from initial survey to signed calculations. This methodical structure ensures structural safety, predictable timescales, and thorough independent verification at every milestone.

Stage 01 Survey and Stage 02 Load Take-Down

Stage 01 Survey requires architectural base plans, historical documentation, and site access. We deliver high-precision laser dimensional surveys, condition logs, and a baseline site note within one to two weeks. Stage 02 Load Take-Down requires intended occupancy schedules and finishes specifications. We produce complete dead, imposed, and wind load distribution schedules within one week. This stage establishes the exact cumulative forces transferring from roof plates down through slabs, columns, and core walls into the underlying ground.

Stage 03 Model and Stage 04 Independent Check

Stage 03 Model requires finalized architectural layouts. Over two to four weeks, our engineers generate three-dimensional finite element models in accordance with Eurocode standards, producing member sizing calculations and deflection profiles. Stage 04 Independent Check requires the completed analysis package. Over one to two weeks, a dedicated checking engineer rebuilds the critical load paths independently to verify stability, shear capacity, and serviceability limits. No calculations proceed to drawing production without this mandatory internal sign-off.

Stage 05 Drawings and Stage 06 Signed Calculations

Stage 05 Drawings translates verified mathematical models into coordinated structural documents over two to three weeks. You receive general arrangement drawings, reinforcement schedules, connection details, and BIM models compliant with ISO 19650. Stage 06 Signed Calculations requires final review of the integrated package. Within three working days, our chartered structural engineer delivers a bound, officially signed calculation package and certificate ready for immediate submission to building control and warranty providers.

What checking categories govern structural verification?

Structural checking categories define the required level of independent scrutiny based on building risk, complexity, and public consequence. Category 1 applies to standard elements and simple single-storey works checked internally by the designer. Category 2 applies to typical multi-storey residential and commercial buildings, requiring checking by an independent engineer within the same practice who was not involved in design. Category 3 governs novel, high-consequence, or complex structures, requiring an entirely separate external engineering firm to produce independent models.

pages.title: Selected Projects
pages.content:
PROJECTS

Selected Projects

Home / Projects

Our portfolio spans civic libraries, multi-storey residential developments, pedestrian bridges, and sensitive warehouse retrofits. Each project demonstrates our commitment to constructable detailing, material efficiency, and rigorous structural analysis.

Case

Calder Quay Library

Completed in 2022, Calder Quay Library is a three-storey civic educational facility combining cross-laminated timber floor panels with a central reinforced concrete core wall. The structural challenge centered on joining prefabricated mass timber elements to a cast core while controlling differential long-term deflections and acoustic isolation. We developed detailed 3D finite element models to coordinate connection brackets and installation sequences. The completed library features open, unpropped interior spaces with exposed timber soffits that satisfy stringent structural fire criteria and acoustic performance requirements.

View the case study

Case

Northfield Row Housing

Completed in 2023, Northfield Row Housing comprises 48 residential homes arranged across a six-storey reinforced concrete flat-slab frame. The engineering challenge required accommodating non-uniform apartment floor layouts without introducing deep transfer beams that would lower ceiling heights. Our engineers performed extensive long-term deflection modeling under Eurocode 2 to verify slab cracking and creep behavior, designing stud shear reinforcement arrays around slender columns. The resulting flat-slab structure allowed continuous flat soffits, simplified mechanical distribution, and rapid floor casting cycles on site.

View the case study

Weir Lane Footbridge

Erected in 2021, the Weir Lane Footbridge is a fabricated structural steel pedestrian bridge spanning 28 meters across an active river channel. The structural challenge involved managing pedestrian-induced dynamic vibrations and controlling thermal expansion across a slender superstructure with limited crane access from the riverbank. We performed comprehensive modal frequency analysis to eliminate resonant vertical acceleration without resorting to mechanical tuned mass dampers. Detailed as a bolted splice assembly, the entire 28 m span was lifted into position during a single scheduled weekend operation.

View the case study

Case

Mill Street Warehouse Retrofit

Delivered in 2024, the Mill Street Warehouse Retrofit converted a four-storey nineteenth-century industrial brick warehouse into modern commercial office workspace. The project required inserting an independent internal structural steel frame to support upgraded floor loadings while stabilizing historic unreinforced perimeter masonry walls. We conducted comprehensive laser surveys and crack pattern appraisals before engineering resin-anchored wall ties and new concrete pad foundations. The completed retrofit preserves original brick facades while providing open, column-free interior floor plates certified for modern commercial occupancy.

View the case study

pages.title: Calder Quay Library: Structural Case Study
pages.content:
CASE

Calder Quay Library: Structural Case Study

Home / Calder Quay Library

Completed in 2022 at Calder Quay, this three-storey civic library pairs cross-laminated timber floor plates with a robust reinforced concrete core wall. Kiban Structural acted as lead structural engineer from concept scheme notes to signed calculations.

Project Facts and Structural System

Calder Quay Library was completed in 2022, providing three storeys of public reading halls, study spaces, and administrative archives. The primary structural system utilizes cross-laminated timber floor slabs supported by perimeter steel edge columns and anchored to an internal reinforced concrete core. This hybrid configuration was selected to reduce embodied carbon while providing the necessary lateral stability against wind actions. Our Calder Quay studio managed the complete structural engineering package through every phase.

The Engineering Challenge

The primary structural challenge was the interaction between dissimilar structural materials. Timber and concrete exhibit markedly different stiffness, thermal expansion coefficients, and moisture movement characteristics. Floor plates required continuous spans of up to nine meters without intermediate props, demanding strict deflection limits to protect internal acoustic glass partitions. In addition, connection detailing had to accommodate tight crane lifting schedules and provide fire-resistance ratings without relying on secondary decorative cladding.

Our Approach and Project Result

We established a detailed three-dimensional finite element model to simulate construction stages, analyzing early creep deflections and interface shear forces between timber panels and the core wall. Custom steel embedment plates were cast directly into the concrete core, allowing timber floor cassettes to drop into place with crane hook releases. The library opened on schedule with certified structural compliance under Eurocode 5 and Eurocode 2, delivering quiet, robust, and beautiful civic architecture.

Back to all projects

pages.title: Northfield Row Housing: Structural Case Study
pages.content:
CASE

Northfield Row Housing: Structural Case Study

Home / Northfield Row Housing

Constructed in 2023, Northfield Row Housing provides 48 high-quality residential apartments within a six-storey reinforced concrete flat-slab structure. Kiban Structural designed the complete frame, foundations, and stability systems.

Project Facts and Structural Scope

Northfield Row Housing was delivered in 2023, creating 48 private residential apartments across six storeys. The structural design specified a cast-in-place reinforced concrete flat slab supported by circular internal columns and robust perimeter core walls. Flat-slab construction was chosen to maximize internal vertical clearances, simplify mechanical service distribution across apartment ceilings, and accelerate the structural construction program on site.

The Engineering Challenge

The fundamental structural challenge lay in managing high punching shear stresses around internal columns while keeping slab depths minimal. Varied apartment layouts between upper residential levels and ground-floor communal amenities created eccentric load paths that threatened long-term slab deflections. Excessive deflection would crack brittle ceramic tile finishes and jam acoustic partition head joints. We needed a solution that eliminated intrusive downstand transfer beams across residential corridors.

Our Approach and Project Result

Our team produced twin computational analysis models to check instantaneous and long-term creep deflections in strict compliance with Eurocode 2. We designed proprietary stud shear reinforcement rails around column heads, avoiding bulky drop panels and maintaining uniform slab thicknesses throughout. The contractor completed frame pours efficiently without transfer beams, and independent site testing verified that slab deflections remained comfortably within design limits, with signed calculations approved by building authorities.

Back to all projects

pages.title: Weir Lane Footbridge: Structural Case Study
pages.content:
CASE

Weir Lane Footbridge: Structural Case Study

Home / Weir Lane Footbridge

Erected in 2021, the Weir Lane Footbridge provides an elegant 28-meter clear span for pedestrians and cyclists crossing an active river channel. Kiban Structural delivered full structural analysis, connection design, and erection engineering.

Project Facts and Structural Arrangement

The Weir Lane Footbridge was commissioned and installed in 2021, providing a dedicated 28-meter pedestrian and cycle link over a river channel. Constructed from fabricated structural steelwork, the superstructure consists of two slender variable-depth longitudinal girders braced by transverse cross-beams and a lightweight deck. Kiban Structural acted as lead structural engineer, responsible for superstructure sizing, abutment foundation design, and site lifting analysis.

The Engineering Challenge

Pedestrian footbridges with spans approaching thirty meters are notoriously susceptible to dynamic vibration caused by footfall synchronization. The bridge deck had to be sufficiently slender to meet planning visual requirements while avoiding harmonic frequencies between 1.5 and 2.5 Hertz. In addition, site constraints were acute: steep, unreinforced riverbanks prevented heavy mobile crane access on one side of the channel, requiring an erection plan using a single-crane lift.

Our Approach and Project Result

We carried out modal vibration analysis in accordance with Eurocode 3 and Eurocode 1 traffic actions, tuning girder geometry and deck mass to push primary natural frequencies well outside human pacing ranges. The steelwork was fabricated off-site in modular sections with high-strength friction-grip bolted splices, enabling rapid assembly on the adjacent roadway before a single 350-tonne crane lift placed the completed 28 m span onto concrete bankseat abutments.

Back to all projects

pages.title: Mill Street Warehouse Retrofit: Structural Case Study
pages.content:
CASE

Mill Street Warehouse Retrofit: Structural Case Study

Home / Mill Street Warehouse Retrofit

Delivered in 2024, this project revitalized a four-storey unreinforced historic brick warehouse for modern commercial workspace. Kiban Structural engineered an internal steel frame and perimeter masonry stabilization system.

Project Facts and Adaptive Scope

The Mill Street Warehouse Retrofit was completed in 2024, successfully adapting a four-storey industrial masonry building originally constructed for heavy textile storage. The client required modern open-plan office accommodation while preserving the external historic brick facades. Kiban Structural provided the full engineering scope: preliminary condition surveys, load take-down calculations, foundation underpinning design, and a complete new internal steel frame.

The Engineering Challenge

The primary engineering challenge stemmed from the fragile condition of existing multi-wythe brick walls bound with deteriorating lime mortar. Removing rotten timber internal joists risked leaving tall perimeter walls unbraced against lateral wind forces during construction. Furthermore, existing shallow stone footings had experienced historic settlement and could not support concentrated modern point loads without substantial strengthening and foundation intervention.

Our Approach and Project Result

We conducted comprehensive on-site laser scanning and mortar condition testing before designing a self-supporting internal steel skeletal frame erected on isolated concrete pad footings. External masonry walls were secured back to new steel floor beams using stainless steel resin-injected ties, restoring lateral stability without altering external appearances. The building was delivered safely to modern loading codes without cracking historic fabric, with signed calculations approved by local building control.

Back to all projects

pages.title: Fee Schedule and Terms
pages.content:
FEES

Fee Schedule and Terms

Home / Fees

At Kiban Structural, we believe engineering fees should be transparent, predictable, and directly tied to project milestones. Our standard schedule of rates provides clear pricing baselines before formal commitments are made.

Schedule of Professional Rates

Our baseline engineering fees are defined as follows: Feasibility & structural scheme note: from €1,800. Site survey & condition report: €950 per site day. Structural design, residential up to 4 storeys: from €9,500. Independent design check: from €3,200. Retrofit assessment & strengthening design: from €4,800. Site inspection visit with written report: €640 per visit. All listed prices are in Euros, exclusive of statutory VAT. Fixed quotes are issued following the completion of an initial structural scheme note.

Scope of Included Services

Every formal commission includes initial architectural model reviews, analytical finite element calculations, dead and live load take-down documentation, coordinated structural drawing packages, internal peer checks, and signed calculation certificates ready for statutory building authority submissions. We attend designated design coordination workshops and respond directly to local authority engineering queries. Specialty invasive investigations, core sampling, and third-party soils testing are excluded from our base fees and are quoted separately when required.

Milestone Payment Schedule

To ensure alignment between deliverables and payment, our project invoicing follows three distinct stages: 30% upon issue of the preliminary structural scheme note, 50% upon delivery of primary engineering calculations and drawing sets, and 20% upon final sign-off and local authority submission. Invoices are payable within fourteen days of issuance. This staged structure ensures clients only pay for verified, delivered engineering milestones throughout their project timeline.

pages.title: Engineering Journal
pages.content:
JOURNAL

Engineering Journal

Home / Journal

Technical observations, field notes, and practical structural principles from our engineers at Kiban Structural. We share insights drawn from active sites, structural surveys, and analytical model reviews.

Reading a Crack Before Repairing It

When a crack opens across a load-bearing wall or concrete beam, cosmetic filling without diagnosing the root cause invites recurring failure. In our practice, we treat cracks as empirical records of stress imbalances. Measuring width, orientation, and movement over time reveals whether damage stems from thermal contraction, foundation settlement, or active structural overloading. Calculations in accordance with Eurocode standards verify remaining capacity, ensuring that strengthening work addresses genuine load paths rather than superficial surface symptoms.

Read the full note

Why We Check Flat Slabs Twice

Reinforced concrete flat slabs provide elegant floor profiles and simplified services routing, but they are unforgiving when dynamic construction loads and long-term creep are underestimated. Punching shear at internal column heads represents a brittle failure mechanism that demands independent calculation. In our Calder Quay studio, every flat-slab model is checked twice by separate engineers: first to verify ultimate bending and shear capacity, and second to model thirty-year creep and deflection behavior.

What a Load Take-Down Is

A load take-down is the methodical accounting of every Newton of force acting upon a building. Starting at the roof ridge, our engineers trace dead loads from permanent materials and live loads from intended building occupancy floor by floor through slabs, beams, columns, and walls down into the supporting subsoil. A disciplined load take-down eliminates guesswork, ensures foundation sizing reflects true cumulative forces, and provides the essential baseline for safe structural design.

pages.title: Frequently Asked Questions
pages.content:
FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Home / FAQ

Common questions regarding our structural engineering services, appointment process, checking standards, and project fees. Contact our Calder Quay studio if your specific question is not addressed below.

When should a structural engineer be appointed on a project?

A structural engineer should ideally be appointed during early architectural concept design. Early involvement allows us to produce a preliminary structural scheme note that tests foundation options, establishes column grids, and identifies key load-bearing walls before layouts are frozen. Appointing an engineer early avoids expensive architectural redesigns, ensures ceiling voids accommodate structural depths, and provides realistic cost data for developer budgets.

What information is needed to issue a fixed fee proposal?

To issue a binding fixed fee proposal, we require architectural plans, elevations, building sections, and a site location map. For existing buildings and retrofit projects, any historical construction drawings, past inspection records, and geotechnical soil reports are also invaluable. With this information, we evaluate structural complexity and issue a clear, itemized proposal detailing deliverables, project stages, and fixed fee amounts.

What is an independent structural check and why is it needed?

An independent structural check is an objective review of design calculations and framing models carried out by an engineer who had no role in producing the original design. It verifies that load paths are continuous, member capacities comply with Eurocode criteria, and deflection limits are respected. Independent checking provides vital quality assurance, satisfying local building control authorities, warranty bodies, and project insurers.

How do you evaluate existing buildings during retrofit appraisals?

We begin retrofit assessments with comprehensive site surveys, measuring structural dimensions, logging existing crack distributions, and checking floor levels. We review archival records to ascertain construction types and identify past unrecorded alterations. Where necessary, we specify targeted material testing before building computational models to verify whether existing masonry walls and timber or steel frames can safely carry updated modern occupancy loads.

What technical codes and design standards do you work to?

All engineering calculations at Kiban Structural are developed in strict compliance with current Eurocodes: Eurocode 0 for basis of design, Eurocode 1 for actions on structures, Eurocode 2 for concrete, Eurocode 3 for steel, Eurocode 5 for timber, Eurocode 7 for geotechnical design, and Eurocode 8 for seismic assessment. Our digital drawings and building models follow ISO 19650 standards.

How long does a typical structural design package take?

Our work follows a structured six-stage process. Stage 01 Survey takes one to two weeks, followed by Stage 02 Load Take-Down in one week. Stage 03 Modeling requires two to four weeks, and Stage 04 Independent Checking takes one to two weeks. Stage 05 Drawings takes two to three weeks, with Stage 06 Signed Calculations delivered within three working days.

What is included in a site inspection visit and written report?

Our site inspection visits are priced at €640 per visit and include an on-site physical review by a chartered structural engineer followed by a formal written report. We inspect reinforcement cages prior to concrete pours, verify connection fit-up in structural steelwork, inspect underpinning works, and investigate unexpected site discoveries. Written reports are issued within forty-eight hours of each site visit.

How are professional fees invoiced across project milestones?

We invoice according to transparent project milestones: 30% upon issue of the initial structural scheme note, 50% upon delivery of primary calculations and drawing sets, and 20% upon final sign-off and building authority submission. For standalone advisory tasks, site survey days are billed at €950 per site day, and condition reports are charged according to our standard schedule.

PRIVACY

Privacy Notice

Home / Privacy

Kiban Structural is committed to protecting the privacy and personal data of our clients, collaborators, and website visitors. This policy outlines how our Calder Quay practice collects, uses, and safeguards information.

Information Collection and Use

We collect only the personal information necessary to communicate effectively with clients and deliver professional structural engineering services. This includes contact names, business addresses, email addresses, telephone numbers, and billing details provided during inquiries and project appointments. We process this information solely to coordinate site visits, draft fee proposals, prepare calculations, and fulfill contractual and statutory building authority obligations.

Project Records, Data Retention, and Security

As chartered structural engineers, we retain project calculation models, structural drawings, site inspection notes, and correspondence for statutory liability periods mandated by building control and professional indemnity insurance requirements. All digital drawing files, BIM models, and client communications are stored securely on access-controlled servers protected by enterprise security protocols. We never sell, transfer, or distribute client contact data to third parties.

posts.title: Reading a Crack Before Repairing It: Structural Diagnosis on Site
posts.excerpt: A structural crack is rarely just surface cosmetic damage, and determining its root cause requires careful examination of load paths, material behavior, and building history before any remedial action begins.
posts.content:
When a crack appears across a masonry wall or along the soffit of a reinforced concrete beam, the immediate instinct on site is often cosmetic repair. Patching, stitching, or injecting resin without understanding why the fracture formed merely conceals an ongoing mechanism. In our engineering practice at Kiban Structural, founded in 2009, we treat every crack as physical evidence of an internal structural dispute between applied stress and material capacity. Understanding that dialogue requires patience, a methodical survey, and an objective load take-down before specifying any structural intervention.

The diagnosis begins with geometric classification. A crack is defined by its width, depth, orientation, and progression over time. Vertical cracks in load-bearing masonry often indicate foundation settlement, thermal contraction, or localized crushing under concentrated joist bearings. Diagonal shear cracks, stepping along mortar beds toward door frames or window corners, suggest uneven subsoil movement or differential loading across adjacent foundations. In reinforced concrete elements, flexural cracks develop perpendicular to primary tension steel at mid-span, while diagonal cracks near supports signal high shear stresses. Measuring crack width with calibrated gauges establishes whether movement is active, seasonal, or long stabilized.

Equally critical is understanding the building history and the sequence of past alterations. Buildings frequently absorb unrecorded alterations over decades of continuous occupation. A partition removed three storeys above, a service penetration cored through a primary beam, or an unintended change in warehouse occupancy loading can redistribute dead and live loads across paths never anticipated in original schemes. When inspecting retrofit projects, such as our work on the Mill Street Warehouse Retrofit in 2024, examining masonry crack patterns helped identify areas where perimeter brickwork had detached from internal floor framing, informing our subsequent steel strengthening designs without unnecessary structural demolition.

Before any remedial repair is detailed, the structural engineer must cross-reference observed physical cracks with mathematical calculations. We verify the member against applicable standards, calculating current dead loads, live loads, and thermal actions in accordance with Eurocode 0, Eurocode 1, and Eurocode 2. This load take-down demonstrates whether the existing cross-section retains adequate capacity or if structural strengthening is required. When calculations confirm that distress arises from historic foundation movement that has ceased, non-structural cosmetic repair may suffice. However, if the crack reflects active overloading or insufficient reinforcement, structural intervention—such as steel tie rods, supplementary framing, or carbon-fiber composite wrap—must be installed and signed off.

Monitoring over time provides the definitive record when initial visual inspection is inconclusive. By installing tell-tale monitors or vibrating-wire strain gauges across critical fractures, movement can be tracked against temperature shifts, groundwater variations, and changing operational occupancy over months. This empirical baseline eliminates guesswork. It prevents both dangerous under-reaction to progressive structural instability and costly over-reaction to benign thermal expansion. Our role as structural engineers is to interpret these measurements with clear technical discipline, ensuring clients receive actionable reports rather than speculative assumptions.

Rushing to cover a crack risks masking structural distress until secondary failures occur elsewhere. A calm, rigorous inspection, supported by dimensional surveys and independent checking, ensures that remedial work addresses root causes rather than symptoms. By verifying physical conditions on site and corroborating findings with precise engineering models, we ensure structures remain safe, serviceable, and thoroughly understood throughout their design lives.
